statement: With dualIndex(h,j,t)=3*h*t^3/2+2*j/(3*t^2), for nonzero real h,t the rational dual phase dualIndex/2-h*t^9/4+j*t^4/6 equals dualPhase(h,dualIndex)+remainder(h,j,t), where remainder=j*t^4/2+4*j^2/(27*h*t)+16*j^3/(729*h^2*t^6). Every nonzero natural h gives period 54*h^2 for wave(dualPhase(h,r)) on natural r. The normalized source forms second, third, fourth obey the explicit rational identities in CubicInverseCell.lean; their dual quotients third/second^3+4/(9*h^2) and (fourth*second-3*third^2)/second^5 equal thirdRemainder and fourthRemainder when h,t,1-u are nonzero. For abs(u)<=1/100 the factors 1-u, 1-9*u+3*u^2, and 1-16*u are positive. For h>0,u nonzero, u*thirdRemainder<0, and for t>0 also u*fourthRemainder>0. The four rational exponent bounds with theta=1/6+1/1354, splitLoss=1/2708, frequencyGain=1/50000 and mixedGain=1/25000 are strictly below 2/3-mixedGain; the endpoint budget also holds. All of this algebra is kernel-checked. It does not assert a formal differentiation theorem for the inverse phase, any exponential-sum estimate, or an asymptotic count. The ledger label awaits advisory statement coverage.

Put beta=1/50000 and delta=1/25000. For every real M>=2, interval I contained in (M,2M], and integers 1<=abs(h)<=M^beta and 1<=abs(j)<=M^(1/3+beta), the sum over odd natural m in I of e(h*m^(3/2)/2+j*m^(2/3)/2) is O(M^(2/3-delta)), uniformly in the stated variables. Here e(x)=exp(2*pi*i*x), and j is nonzero. For the actual odd-predecessor multiplicity w(m)=ceil(((m+1)^(2/3)-1)/2)-ceil((m^(2/3)-1)/2), the sum over odd m in I of w(m)*e(h*m^(3/2)/2) is O(M^(2/3-beta)) over the same h range. Its parity-sign version is O(M^(2/3-1/100000)). The proof removes the rational cubic of period 54*h^2, verifies a nonzero monotone third derivative of the remainder, combines the classical third-derivative test with Robert 2005, and retains the sum-length and shifted-endpoint costs. These are AI-assisted written analytic proofs, pending independent review. The resulting short OOO count is weaker than Paper B's existing count; no published exponent, deeper selected-source estimate, growing-depth pressure, escape theorem, or termination theorem follows.
